title_en: Throttle position sensor A: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Throttle Position Sensor / Switch A Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) cannot get a reliable reading of how far the throttle is open.
likely_causes_en: Worn or faulty throttle position sensor
Damaged wiring or loose connector at the sensor
Sensor loose or out of position on the throttle body
rider_advice_en: Idle may be uneven and the throttle may feel jerky. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: idle may be uneven; avoid traffic and long trips
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor connector for water, corrosion and bent pins
Wiggle the harness while watching the throttle reading on the scan tool
Look for a smooth reading from closed to fully open

title_en: Intake manifold pressure (MAP) sensor: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Manifold Absolute Pressure / Barometric Pressure Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) cannot get a reliable reading of intake air pressure, so it cannot judge engine load properly.
likely_causes_en: Loose or cracked hose or seal at the sensor (if hose-fed)
rider_advice_en: The engine may run rough, lose power or be hard to start; get it checked soon. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: may run rough or start hard; ride gently, no long trips
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor hose (if hose-fed) or seal for cracks and loose ends
Compare the pressure reading at key-on with the outside air pressure
Check the connector and wiring for water and corrosion

title_en: Engine oil temperature sensor: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Engine Oil Temperature Sensor Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) cannot get a reliable engine oil temperature reading.
rider_advice_en: The bike should ride normally, but the oil temperature reading is missing or unreliable. Ask a mechanic to check the sensor at the next service.
can_ride_reason: sensor reading only; the bike should run normally
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for oil, heat damage and corrosion
Compare with the engine temperature reading after a cold start

title_en: Oxygen (O2) sensor, upstream: circuit fault
standard_title_en: O2 Sensor Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) cannot get a reliable reading from the exhaust oxygen sensor, so it cannot fine-tune the fuel mixture.
likely_causes_en: Sensor wiring chafed against the exhaust
rider_advice_en: The bike may use more fuel and fail an emission check. It usually rides normally, but get it checked soon to protect the emission system.
can_ride_reason: fuel control changes to a fixed setting; usually rideable
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor harness for melting or chafing near the exhaust
Check the connector for water and corrosion
Watch the sensor reading switch between rich and lean when warm

title_en: Oxygen sensor heater (upstream): circuit fault
standard_title_en: O2 Sensor Heater Circuit Malfunction (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the heater circuit of the oxygen sensor, so the sensor warms up slowly or not at all.
likely_causes_en: Open heater element in the oxygen sensor
Blown heater fuse or faulty relay (if fitted)
rider_advice_en: Fuel mixture control is delayed after starting, so emissions and fuel use may rise. Get it checked soon; the bike usually rides normally.
can_ride_reason: only slows mixture control after start; usually rideable
technician_hints_en: Check the heater fuse or relay, if fitted
Check the sensor connector for water and corrosion
Confirm the sensor starts working soon after a cold start

title_en: Fuel injector, cylinder 1: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Injector Circuit Malfunction — Cylinder 1
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the cylinder 1 injector circuit, so that cylinder may get no fuel or the wrong amount.
likely_causes_en: Fault in the ECU injector driver (less common)
rider_advice_en: The engine may misfire, lose power or stop; on a two-cylinder bike it may keep running on one cylinder, but have it checked soon. Pull over safely, switch off and do not keep riding; have the bike taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: that cylinder may get no fuel and the engine may stop; arrange transport
technician_hints_en: Check the injector connector for water, corrosion and bent pins
Listen for the injector clicking while cranking
Check the injector wiring for chafing

title_en: Ignition coil A, cylinder 1: primary or secondary circuit fault
standard_title_en: Ignition Coil A Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the ignition coil A circuit for cylinder 1, so the spark may be weak or missing.
likely_causes_en: Failed ignition coil (open or shorted winding)
Fault in the ECU ignition driver (less common)
rider_action_basis: spark loss may stop the engine
rider_advice_en: The engine may misfire, lose power or stop; on a two-cylinder bike it may keep running on one cylinder, but have it checked soon. Pull over safely, switch off and do not keep riding; have the bike taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: spark loss can stop the engine; arrange transport
technician_hints_en: Check the coil connector for water and corrosion
On a two-coil bike, swap the coils to see if the fault moves
Check the ignition wiring for chafing

title_en: Fuel pump control: primary circuit fault
standard_title_en: Fuel Pump Primary Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the primary circuit that switches the fuel pump, so the pump may not run.
rider_action_basis: no fuel: may stall or not start
rider_advice_en: The engine may be hard to start or may stop without warning. Pull over safely, switch off and do not keep riding; have the bike taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: pump loss can stop the engine without warning
technician_hints_en: Listen for the fuel pump running for a few seconds at key-on
Check the relay (if fitted) and the connectors for corrosion
Check the pump wiring for chafing and loose connectors

title_en: Crankshaft position sensor A: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Crankshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the crankshaft position sensor circuit, so it may not know engine position.
likely_causes_en: Damaged or dirty toothed ring on the crankshaft
rider_action_basis: engine may stall or not start
rider_advice_en: The engine may stop or not start. Pull over safely, switch off and do not keep riding; have the bike taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: engine may stall or not start; arrange transport
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor connector and wiring for heat damage and oil
Check the toothed ring (reluctor ring) for damaged teeth or metal debris
Check that engine speed shows on the scan tool while cranking

title_en: Intake air temperature sensor: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) cannot get a reliable intake air temperature reading, so it cannot correct the fuelling for air temperature.
rider_advice_en: The bike usually rides normally, though cold starting or fuel use may be slightly off. Get the sensor checked at the next service.
can_ride_reason: minor fuelling error only
technician_hints_en: Check the connector for water and corrosion
Compare the reading with the outside air temperature on a cold bike

title_en: Engine (coolant) temperature sensor: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) cannot get a reliable engine temperature reading, so it cannot tell how hot the engine is.
rider_action_basis: hard cold start or wrong idle
rider_advice_en: The bike may be hard to start when cold or idle badly. Get it checked soon; if the engine runs very hot, stop and let it cool.
can_ride_reason: hard cold start; short trip, avoid very hot weather
technician_hints_en: Check the connector for coolant seepage, water and corrosion
Compare the scan tool reading with the real engine temperature, cold and warm

title_en: Fuel injector, cylinder 2: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Injector Circuit Malfunction — Cylinder 2
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the cylinder 2 injector circuit, so that cylinder may get no fuel or the wrong amount.
rider_action_basis: one cylinder has no fuel; power is reduced
rider_advice_en: One cylinder may get no fuel, so the engine may shake and lose power. Ride gently and keep the trip short; stop if it runs very rough or loses power badly.
can_ride_reason: reduced power and vibration; ride gently, short trip
technician_hints_en: Check the injector connector for water, corrosion and bent pins
Listen for the injector clicking while cranking

title_en: Ignition coil B, cylinder 2: primary or secondary circuit fault
standard_title_en: Ignition Coil B Primary/Secondary Circuit Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the ignition coil B circuit for cylinder 2, so the spark may be weak or missing.
likely_causes_en: Failed ignition coil (open or shorted winding)
rider_action_basis: spark loss on one cylinder; power is reduced
rider_advice_en: The spark on one cylinder may be weak or missing, so the engine may shake and lose power. Ride gently and keep the trip short; stop if it runs very rough or loses power badly.
can_ride_reason: reduced power and vibration; ride gently, short trip
technician_hints_en: Check the coil connector for water and corrosion
Swap the coils to see if the fault moves to the other cylinder
Check the ignition wiring for chafing

title_en: Random or multiple cylinder misfire detected
standard_title_en: Random/Multiple Cylinder Misfire Detected
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) detected misfires on more than one cylinder or at random, so combustion is incomplete.
likely_causes_en: Low fuel pressure or weak fuel supply
rider_advice_en: Expect rough running, jerking or loss of power. Ride gently, avoid hard acceleration and get it checked soon; stop if it runs very rough, backfires or loses power badly.
can_ride_reason: ride gently, avoid hard acceleration; keep the trip short
technician_hints_en: Read the freeze-frame data to see when the misfire happens
Check the spark plugs and ignition coils first
Check for intake air leaks and fuel supply problems

title_en: Cylinder 1 misfire detected
standard_title_en: Cylinder 1 Misfire Detected
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) detected misfires on cylinder 1, so that cylinder is not burning its fuel properly.
likely_causes_en: Worn or fouled spark plug on cylinder 1
Blocked or leaking injector on cylinder 1
rider_advice_en: Expect rough running, jerking or loss of power. Ride gently, avoid hard acceleration and get it checked soon; stop if it runs very rough, backfires or loses power badly.
can_ride_reason: ride gently, avoid hard acceleration; keep the trip short
technician_hints_en: Read the freeze-frame data to see when the misfire happens
Check the spark plug and ignition coil on this cylinder first
Check the injector and compression if spark is good

title_en: Cylinder 2 misfire detected
standard_title_en: Cylinder 2 Misfire Detected
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) detected misfires on cylinder 2, so that cylinder is not burning its fuel properly.
likely_causes_en: Worn or fouled spark plug on cylinder 2
Blocked or leaking injector on cylinder 2
rider_advice_en: Expect rough running, jerking or loss of power. Ride gently, avoid hard acceleration and get it checked soon; stop if it runs very rough, backfires or loses power badly.
can_ride_reason: ride gently, avoid hard acceleration; keep the trip short
technician_hints_en: Read the freeze-frame data to see when the misfire happens
Check the spark plug and ignition coil on this cylinder first
Check the injector if spark is good

title_en: Fuel mixture too lean
standard_title_en: System Too Lean (Bank 1)
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) is adding extra fuel to keep the mixture right, so the engine is getting too much air or too little fuel.
likely_causes_en: Weak fuel pump or low fuel pressure
rider_advice_en: The engine may hesitate, run rough or lose power, and a lean mixture can overheat the engine. Get it checked soon and avoid hard or long rides until it is fixed.
can_ride_reason: lean mixture can overheat the engine; short, gentle ride only
technician_hints_en: Look for cracked intake boots and loose clamps
Check fuel supply and injector condition
Compare the fuel trim values at idle and at steady cruise

title_en: Fuel mixture too rich
standard_title_en: System Too Rich (Bank 1)
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) is removing fuel to keep the mixture right, which means the engine is getting too much fuel or too little air.
rider_action_basis: rich mixture can harm emission system
rider_advice_en: Expect black smoke or poor mileage; get it checked soon. If you smell petrol strongly near the engine or tank, or see fuel dripping, stop and do not ride.
can_ride_reason: only if no strong petrol smell and no fuel dripping
technician_hints_en: Check the air filter and intake for blockage
Check for fuel leakage at the injector and fuel line
Check that the oxygen sensor reading is changing

title_en: Catalytic converter efficiency below threshold
standard_title_en: Catalyst System Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) judges that the catalytic converter is not cleaning the exhaust as well as expected.
likely_causes_en: Modified, damaged or removed exhaust or converter
Exhaust leak before the catalytic converter
rider_advice_en: The bike usually rides normally, but emissions may be above the limit. Get it checked at the next service; fix any misfire first.
can_ride_reason: emissions only; the bike should run normally
technician_hints_en: Ask whether the exhaust or converter was changed, damaged or removed
Check for exhaust leaks before the catalytic converter
Compare the upstream and downstream oxygen sensor readings

title_en: Throttle position sensor A: voltage below threshold
standard_title_en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Low Input
meaning_en: The throttle position reading is too low for the bike's computer (ECU), often from a short to ground or a missing sensor supply.
likely_causes_en: Sensor supply missing at the connector
rider_advice_en: The bike may idle badly, hesitate or lose power. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: ECU may limit power; avoid traffic and long trips
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for chafing, water and corrosion
Check that the sensor supply and ground reach the connector
Watch the throttle reading on the scan tool while turning the throttle

title_en: Throttle position sensor A: voltage above threshold
standard_title_en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" High Input
meaning_en: The throttle position reading is too high for the bike's computer (ECU), often from a short to battery supply or a broken sensor ground.
likely_causes_en: Signal wire short to battery supply
rider_advice_en: The bike may idle high or badly, hesitate or lose power. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: ECU may limit power; avoid traffic and long trips
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for chafing, water and corrosion
Check the sensor ground connection
Watch the throttle reading on the scan tool while turning the throttle

title_en: Intake manifold pressure (MAP) sensor: voltage below threshold
standard_title_en: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Low Input
meaning_en: The intake pressure reading is too low for the bike's computer (ECU), often from a short to ground or a missing sensor supply.
likely_causes_en: Sensor supply missing at the connector
rider_advice_en: The engine may run rough, lose power or be hard to start; get it checked soon. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: may run rough or start hard; ride gently, no long trips
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for chafing, water and corrosion
Compare the pressure reading at key-on with the outside air pressure

title_en: Intake manifold pressure (MAP) sensor: voltage above threshold
standard_title_en: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor High Input
meaning_en: The intake pressure reading is too high for the bike's computer (ECU), often from a short to battery supply or a broken sensor ground.
likely_causes_en: Signal wire short to battery supply
rider_advice_en: The engine may use too much fuel, lose power or be hard to start; get it checked soon. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: may run rough or start hard; ride gently, no long trips
technician_hints_en: Check the connector and wiring for chafing, water and corrosion
Compare the pressure reading at key-on with the outside air pressure

title_en: Intake air temperature sensor: voltage below threshold
standard_title_en: Intake Air Temperature Sensor Low Input
meaning_en: The intake air temperature signal is too low for the bike's computer (ECU), so the air looks hotter than it is.
rider_advice_en: The bike usually rides normally, though fuel use or cold starting may be slightly off. Get the sensor checked at the next service.
can_ride_reason: minor fuelling error only
technician_hints_en: Check the wiring for chafing and the connector for water
Compare the reading with the outside air temperature on a cold bike

title_en: Intake air temperature sensor: voltage above threshold
standard_title_en: Intake Air Temperature Sensor High Input
meaning_en: The intake air temperature signal is higher than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, so the air looks colder than it is; often an open circuit.
likely_causes_en: Open circuit in the sensor or wiring
rider_advice_en: The bike usually rides normally, though fuel use or cold starting may be slightly off. Get the sensor checked at the next service.
can_ride_reason: minor fuelling error only
technician_hints_en: Check the connector for corrosion and a loose fit
Compare the reading with the outside air temperature on a cold bike

title_en: Engine (coolant) temperature sensor: voltage below threshold
standard_title_en: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor Low Input
meaning_en: The engine temperature signal is lower than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, so the engine looks hotter than it is; often a short to ground.
rider_action_basis: hard cold start; runs unevenly until warm
rider_advice_en: The bike may be hard to start when cold and run unevenly until warm. Get it checked soon; if it runs very hot, stop and let it cool.
can_ride_reason: hard cold start; short trip, avoid very hot weather
technician_hints_en: Check the wiring for chafing and the connector for water
Compare the scan tool reading with the real engine temperature on a cold engine

title_en: Engine (coolant) temperature sensor: voltage above threshold
standard_title_en: Engine Coolant Temperature Sensor High Input
meaning_en: The engine temperature signal is higher than the bike's computer (ECU) expects, so the engine looks colder than it is; often an open circuit.
likely_causes_en: Open circuit in the sensor or wiring
rider_action_basis: extra fuel use; cooling may not switch on
rider_advice_en: The bike may use more fuel and smoke, and cooling may not switch on when needed. Get it checked soon; if the engine runs very hot, stop and let it cool.
can_ride_reason: cooling may not switch on when needed; avoid traffic and heat
technician_hints_en: Check the connector for corrosion and a loose fit
Compare the scan tool reading with the real engine temperature on a warm engine

title_en: Oxygen (O2) sensor, upstream: voltage below threshold
standard_title_en: O2 Sensor Circuit Low Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
meaning_en: The oxygen sensor reading stays low, which can come from a lean mixture, an exhaust leak or a short to ground.
likely_causes_en: Lean running (air leak or low fuel supply)
rider_advice_en: The engine may hesitate or run rough, and emissions may rise. Get it checked soon; the bike usually rides normally.
can_ride_reason: usually rideable; mixture control only affected
technician_hints_en: Check the exhaust joints before the sensor for leaks
Check the sensor wiring for chafing near the exhaust
Check for intake air leaks and low fuel supply

title_en: Oxygen (O2) sensor, upstream: voltage above threshold
standard_title_en: O2 Sensor Circuit High Voltage (Bank 1, Sensor 1)
meaning_en: The oxygen sensor reading stays high, which can come from a rich mixture, a contaminated sensor or a short to battery supply.
likely_causes_en: Rich running (leaking injector or high fuel pressure)
Signal wire short to battery supply
Sensor contaminated by silicone or coolant
rider_advice_en: Expect poor mileage or black smoke; get it checked soon. If you smell petrol strongly near the engine or tank, or see fuel dripping, stop and do not ride.
can_ride_reason: usually rideable; not with strong petrol smell or dripping fuel
technician_hints_en: Check the injectors and fuel pressure for a rich condition
Check the sensor wiring for chafing and heat damage
Look for silicone sealant or coolant contamination

title_en: Vehicle speed sensor A: fault
standard_title_en: Vehicle Speed Sensor "A" Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) is not getting a reliable vehicle speed signal.
rider_advice_en: The speedometer may read wrongly or not at all, and other speed-based functions may be affected. Get it checked soon and do not rely on the speedometer.
can_ride_reason: speedometer may be unreliable; ride carefully
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor connector and wiring for damage and water
Compare the speed shown on the scan tool with the speedometer

title_en: System voltage below threshold (battery or charging)
standard_title_en: System Voltage Low
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) sees the electrical system voltage lower than expected, so the battery may be weak or charging may be poor.
likely_causes_en: Corroded battery terminals or loose ground
rider_advice_en: Lights may dim and the bike may be hard to start. If the battery goes flat while riding the engine will stop, so avoid night and long rides and get the charging checked soon.
can_ride_reason: a flat battery stops the engine; go straight to a workshop, no night rides
technician_hints_en: Check the battery terminals and ground connections for corrosion and looseness
Check battery condition and charging at idle and at higher engine speed

title_en: System voltage above threshold (overcharging)
standard_title_en: System Voltage High
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) sees the electrical system voltage higher than expected, so the charging system may be overcharging.
rider_action_basis: overcharge can boil battery; daylight ride only
rider_advice_en: If the battery is hot, swollen or smells of rotten eggs, stop, switch off and do not ride on. Do the same if the lights are very bright or bulbs keep blowing. Otherwise ride only a short way, in daylight, to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: short daylight ride only; stop at once if the battery is hot or swollen
technician_hints_en: Check the charging level at idle and at higher engine speed
Check the regulator connector for heat damage and corrosion

title_en: Neutral switch input: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Park/Neutral Switch Input Circuit
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) may not know whether the bike is in neutral, because the neutral switch signal is faulty.
likely_causes_en: Switch loose or out of position
rider_action_basis: start or idle behaviour may be wrong
rider_advice_en: Starting or idle behaviour may change when the bike cannot tell if it is in neutral. Get it checked soon; if it will not start, do not bypass any safety switch.
can_ride_reason: if it starts, go straight to a workshop and do not bypass switches
technician_hints_en: Check that the neutral status on the scan tool changes when the gear is selected
Check the switch connector for oil, water and corrosion
Check the switch wiring for chafing

title_en: Serial communication link: fault
standard_title_en: Serial Communication Link
meaning_en: The bike's electronic units cannot talk to each other properly over their communication link.
likely_causes_en: Damaged wiring on the communication lines
rider_advice_en: Warning lamps or other functions may not work correctly; get it checked soon. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: effect unclear; stop if the engine misbehaves
technician_hints_en: Check the connectors and wiring on the communication lines for water and chafing
Read all control units for related communication codes
Check the ground and supply connections of the control units

title_en: Camshaft position sensor A: circuit fault
standard_title_en: Camshaft Position Sensor "A" Circuit (Bank 1 or Single Sensor)
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) found a fault in the camshaft position sensor circuit, so it may not time fuel and spark correctly.
rider_action_basis: may start hard or run rough
rider_advice_en: The engine may be hard to start, run rough or lose power; get it checked soon. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: may start hard or run rough; short trip only
technician_hints_en: Check the sensor connector and wiring for oil, heat damage and corrosion
Check the sensor mounting and its signal while cranking

title_en: Idle control system: fault
standard_title_en: Idle Control System Malfunction
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) cannot hold the engine idle speed where it wants it.
likely_causes_en: Sticky or dirty idle air control valve
Air leak after the throttle (vacuum leak)
rider_action_basis: idle speed may be too high or too low
rider_advice_en: If it stalls once at a stop, ride gently, avoid heavy traffic and have it checked soon. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding.
can_ride_reason: idle may be unsteady; avoid heavy traffic and long trips
technician_hints_en: Clean the throttle body and idle air passage as the service manual says
Check for intake air leaks
Compare commanded and actual idle speed on the scan tool

title_en: Engine computer (ECU): communication lost
standard_title_en: Lost Communication with ECM/PCM "A"
meaning_en: Another unit on the bike stopped receiving messages from the engine computer (ECU), because the ECU is off or its link is broken.
likely_causes_en: ECU not getting power (fuse if fitted, ground, supply)
Broken communication wiring to the ECU
rider_action_basis: engine computer or its link; two cases
rider_advice_en: If the engine runs normally, have it checked soon; if it stalls, loses power or will not start, do not keep riding.
can_ride_reason: ride only if the engine runs normally, straight to a workshop
technician_hints_en: Check the ECU fuse (if fitted), ground and supply connections
Check the communication wiring and connectors for damage
Check whether other control units also show communication lost codes

title_en: ABS control unit: communication lost
standard_title_en: Lost Communication with ABS Control Module
meaning_en: Another control unit on the bike stopped receiving messages from the ABS control unit, so ABS is likely off.
likely_causes_en: ABS unit not getting power (fuse if fitted, ground)
Broken communication wiring to the ABS unit
rider_advice_en: Your normal brakes still work, but ABS is off, so a wheel can lock in hard braking. Ride gently, brake early and get it checked soon.
can_ride_reason: brakes work but no ABS; ride gently, brake early, avoid wet roads
technician_hints_en: Check the ABS fuse (if fitted), ground and supply connections
Check the communication wiring and connectors for damage
Check whether the speedometer also stops (some bikes take speed from the ABS unit)

title_en: Instrument cluster: communication lost
standard_title_en: Lost Communication with Instrument Panel Cluster
meaning_en: The bike's computer (ECU) or another unit stopped receiving messages from the instrument cluster.
likely_causes_en: Cluster not getting power (fuse if fitted, poor ground)
Broken communication wiring to the cluster
rider_action_basis: meters and lamps may not work
rider_advice_en: The speedometer and warning lamps may not work, so you may miss a warning. Get it checked soon and ride carefully.
can_ride_reason: without lamps you may miss a warning; ride carefully
technician_hints_en: Check the cluster fuse (if fitted), ground and supply connections
Check the communication wiring and connectors for damage

title_en: Throttle position sensor A: performance or incorrect operation
standard_title_en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Range/Performance
meaning_en: The throttle position reading does not match what the bike's computer (ECU) expects, so the throttle opening may be misread.
likely_causes_en: Worn or faulty throttle position sensor
Sensor loose or out of position on the throttle body
rider_advice_en: The bike may idle badly, hesitate or jerk. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: idle may be uneven; avoid traffic and long trips
technician_hints_en: Compare the throttle reading with the real throttle position, closed to fully open
Check the sensor mounting and the connector for water and corrosion

title_en: Throttle position sensor A: intermittent circuit fault
standard_title_en: Throttle/Pedal Position Sensor "A" Circuit Intermittent
meaning_en: The throttle position reading is lost or changes suddenly at times, so the bike's computer (ECU) sometimes misreads the throttle.
likely_causes_en: Loose or corroded connector at the sensor
Chafed wiring that breaks contact at times
Worn or faulty throttle position sensor
rider_advice_en: The bike may hesitate, jerk or idle badly at times. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
can_ride_reason: throttle may misbehave at times; avoid traffic and long trips
technician_hints_en: Wiggle the harness and connector while watching the throttle reading on the scan tool
Look for sudden changes in the reading while moving the throttle slowly

title_en: Intake pressure (MAP) sensor: performance or incorrect operation
standard_title_en: Manifold Absolute Pressure Sensor Range/Performance
meaning_en: The intake pressure reading does not match engine conditions, so the bike's computer (ECU) may misjudge engine load.
likely_causes_en: Faulty or slow intake pressure (MAP) sensor
Air leak after the throttle (vacuum leak)
Blocked or loose hose or seal at the sensor (if hose-fed)
rider_advice_en: The engine may run rough, lose power or be hard to start; get it checked soon. If it stalls more than once or will not restart, do not keep riding; have it taken to a workshop.
